question: Lll and Mmm run a café. They start with 214 servings. They lose 192 (22). They multiply by 9 (198). They multiply by 6 (1188). They add 36 (1224). One distractor: capacity is 1300. How many servings?
Rrr and Sss manage a warehouse. They start with 136 items. They multiply by 8 (1088). They add 57 (1145). They divide by 5 (229). They add 20 (249). One distractor: capacity was 500. How many items?

A clinic starts with 140 patients. In the morning, 114 leave (26). By midday, 54 arrive (80). By afternoon, 45 arrive (125). By evening, 20 leave (105). It adds 18 (123). All stages track one patient count. How many patients?

A studio started with 48 minutes of footage. They created 6 platform versions multiplying by 6 total. They removed 52 minutes of corrupted data. Each minute expanded into 9 clips. They made 4 backup copies. Then they consolidated all 4 backups into 1 master archive. How many minutes remained in the final archive?

Sarah counted 57 items in her shop each morning. She divided them into 3 sections equally. By afternoon one section lost 17 items. Late afternoon she tripled section amounts. A customer donated 17 items. A supplier delivered new stock but only 1 qualified. By closing she multiplied her count by 9 for weekly projection. What was her projected weekly count?

A restaurant owner started the week with 224 kilograms of supplies. Monday she used 98 kilograms. Tuesday she used 99 more kilograms. She tripled her remaining stock as backup. Emergency supplies cost 37 kilograms. A wholesale delivery added 74 kilograms. A similar restaurant had 2 metric tons in separate items. How many kilograms did she have at the end?

A library started with 193 donated books. A school added 48 books. The library removed 157 duplicate books. A donor contributed 45 additional books. A community center added 51 more books. The library had cataloging supplies worth 220 items tracked separately. What was the final book collection total?

Marcus and Elena competed in trivia. Marcus started with 164 points. Round one he lost 50 points. Round two he lost 98 more. Then he earned 27 points. He gained 54 additional points. His total multiplied by 7 for championship. Elena started with 120 points separately. What was Marcus's final score?

A farmer started with 95 kilograms of grain. He multiplied harvest by 4 times. He sold 16 kilograms at market. He purchased 8 kilograms of premium seed. He stored 21 more kilograms from another harvest. His grain was approximately 0.39 metric tons total. How many kilograms did he have?

A musician earned 184 dollars from her first performance. She added 8 dollars in tips. A contract multiplied earnings by 8. The event organizer multiplied all artist earnings by 4. She added 19 final dollars in fan tips. Her road manager had 45 dollars in separate expenses. What was her final earnings total?

Chen started an event with 69 points. He scored 50 additional points. He lost 23 points on penalty. He earned 9 times that through achievement. He received 33 bonus points. His final score multiplied by 7 for championship ranking. His teammate started with 45 points differently. What was Chen's final championship score?

A farmer started with 151 animals. He multiplied by 5 for herd. He multiplied by 2 for breeding projection. He lost 875 to illness. An auction sold 223 more animals. He multiplied remaining by 5 for next year's breeding plan. His neighbor had 200 animals separately. How many animals did he project for next year?

Patrick the investor started with 98 dollars. He earned 71 in dividends. He earned 34 more dollars. Returns tripled due to growth. He received 14 bonus dollars. He added 16 more in contributions. His partner invested 120 separately. What was Patrick's final investment total?

A researcher tracked data starting at 204 units. It divided by 6 for calibration. She added 38 from secondary measurement. She subtracted 31 for error correction. She multiplied by 6 to scale up. She multiplied by 2 for final projection. The result was 0.492 thousand units total. What was her final data value?

A project started with 229 dollars budget. They multiplied by 8 for seasonal expansion. Project costs reduced it by 293 dollars. New funding added 51 dollars. The final budget doubled. A neighboring project had 310 dollars separately. What was the doubled project budget?

A bakery had 138 pastries at opening. They baked 76 more items by mid-morning (214 pastries). Some items sold, reducing inventory by 18 (196 pastries). A delivery added 15 more pastries (211 pastries). A final 10 items were delivered by afternoon. Converting their inventory from units to approximate dozens, they had about 18 dozen pastries. A neighboring shop had 95 pastries but tracked separately. How many pastries did the bakery have?

A morning run started with 144 kilometers of planned route. By mid-morning, runners reduced the course by 44 kilometers (100 km). In the afternoon session, another 10 kilometers were removed due to weather (90 km). Late afternoon brought 21 kilometers of additional routes (111 km). By evening, the total distance was multiplied by 7 for the weekly training plan. There were 87 competitors registered but this didn't affect the distance. What was the total weekly distance?

A small farm started with 17 chickens. They increased the flock by a factor of 5 through breeding (85 chickens). Two died during the season (83 chickens). A farmer purchased 54 more birds (137 chickens). Many chickens were sold off, reducing the flock by 136 birds. Converting to dozens, the remaining flock was about 0.08 dozen. The farm had originally housed double the starting amount in an old barn. How many chickens remained?

A gardener started with 104 plants. She removed 31 diseased plants (73 plants). She then multiplied her healthy plants by 6 through propagation (438 plants). She divided them in half between two gardens (219 plants each). She then planted 168 of them in the main garden beds. Converting her plants to dozens per section, this represented about 4.3 dozen. How many plants did she have remaining in the propagation area?

A student had 39 homework problems to complete. In the morning, she finished 27 problems (12 remaining). By early afternoon, she completed 4 more problems (8 remaining). After a break, she finished 4 additional problems (4 remaining). Late afternoon brought 2 more problems somehow (2 remaining). She then found 6 bonus problems to work on (8 problems total). By evening, she attempted to double her attempts. What was her total evening count?

A store manager tracked daily sales. Starting with 163 dollars in inventory value, he doubled his stock (326 dollars). Major sales reduced this by 324 dollars (2 dollars). He restocked and multiplied by 6 (12 dollars). Morning rush sales added 14 dollars (26 dollars). Afternoon sales added 28 more dollars. A warehouse 50 kilometers away held different inventory. What was the final sales total?

A gym class started with 41 participants. In the morning session, 14 students didn't show up (27 participants). By mid-morning, 6 late arrivals joined (33 participants). In the afternoon session, 74 additional students participated (107 participants total across sessions). By evening, 90 students left the facility (17 remaining). Converting participants to dozens for registration, this was 1.4 dozen students. How many students remained at the end?

Two athletes compared their performance metrics. Starting with 190 total training points, an athlete multiplied by completing 9 workout sessions (1710 points). Results were divided by 6 for official ranking (285 points). The athlete earned 24 bonus points (309 points). An additional 8 points came from a new achievement (317 points). His competitor had 156 training points. What was the final score?

James tracked his project timeline in days. He started with 127 days available. He reduced by 80 days for already completed phases (47 days). He then multiplied by 7 to account for iterations (329 days). He multiplied by 7 again for the full project cycle (2303 days). He received 35 additional days in an extension. Sarah had 89 days on her competing project. What was James's total timeline?

A farmer tracked crops through the day. Starting with 215 bushels in the morning, 88 were sold at market (127 bushels). A supplier added 41 bushels (168 bushels). The harvest was multiplied by 6 through the afternoon collection (1008 bushels). After processing, 210 bushels were stored (798 bushels). By evening, 75 more bushels arrived. A nearby farm had 300 bushels separate from this count. How many total bushels did the farmer have?
